chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Famous Door with Art Tatum and the NBC Piano Playhouse
summary: McRae worked three months at the Famous Door where Billie Holiday followed, and watched Art Tatum on the NBC Piano Playhouse.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Because after I had came back -- now this puts it altogether. After I had came back with the Lunceford thing, I came back and I was still doing some writing. I always went back to that writing that rock and roll stuff, you know. Rhythm and blues back there, you know. And Moe Gale wanted me to -- I think I went on the street for Moe Gale at the Famous Door with Art Tatum. I worked there for three months.
Yeah. That was the winter of 1944, because in '45 -- '44 --
Around January of '44.
Yeah, yeah. Because after

we came out of that Billie Holiday -- Joe Glaser had took Billie Holiday under his wing -- and she followed us in there.
And I went up to see her and I was talking to her, you know. After we had closed, she followed us in the Famous Door.
That was the time that Art Tatum -- when I was hanging out with Art Tatum and he was doing the piano playhouse from New York.
And I was going down there every Sunday with him to listen to these great piano players, and they was bringing all these piano players in.

The whole time that we were at the Famous Door, Art Tatum was doing this piano Playhouse. Now, I used to (inaudible) get up Sunday morning and go down to NBC at Radio City and watch (inaudible) the Piano Playhouse.
Had these two white girls, they were a team. Then they would bring in another concert piano -- they would bring Art Tatum -- and they would this jamming in there. (Tatum inaudible) would play --

The two piano players on the show, they would play. Then the other concert piano player would come out and do his thing. He would (inaudible). Always (inaudible) brought in concert piano players. Then Art Tatum would be there. He'd be the guest star.
They would do a rhythm thing like Dinah. They would do any pop thing -- rhythm thing, or something like that.
And the two guys on the staff, they would play together, then the concert piano would play it, then Art Tatum would play it.
When they got down to Art Tatum, the house would come down, because Art Tatum would be playing.

Then all four of them would play it together. The two piano players (inaudible) and would be like feeding him the concert piano, he's running, and Art Tatum is running through everybody. And they all wind up together (inaudible) Art Tatum.
And after that -- must have been to hear
Fantastic (inaudible) --

Yeah. Oh, it was fantastic. It was really fantastic. And they got all those tapes down there. I wish they would release them so people could hear some of that stuff.
What studios were these in?
NBC. Piano Playhouse. All that Art Tatum stuff they have --
The transcription is there more than likely.
Yeah. They should release some of that stuff so people could really --
Take a while --

They should release it to the colleges -- places like that. If they don't want it on the market, put it... here where they should (inaudible) the students can hear some of that stuff. It would be a great help to them. I don't know why they don't release that stuff to the colleges, (inaudible) and Institutes jazz things like that, you know.
